items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: So I listened to him play and sing for a long time, and then he used to play for me and let me sing. He said I could sing pretty good, so I used to try to sing like him.

ctx.x: So I learnt by sittin' down listenin' to different people play and listen to 'em sing. Was a man called Slam Stewart who was a helluva piano player and could sing up a storm. So I finally started hanging out with him. So I run get his cigars for him, do little odd jobs, whatever he wanted, I was right there. I was his boy. So I could slip in anywhere he worked at.

He had a piano at his house, too. So I go by there in the daytime and listen to him play and sing. He be practicin'. He always have three or four people in his house. They be drinkin' beer, havin' a good time. So I listened to him play and sing for a long time, and then he used to play for me and let me sing. He said I could sing pretty good, so I used to try to sing like him.

All in the meantime, I was thinkin' of it all the time. I was thinkin' how I was gonna be get into the nightclub where he worked at 'cause I was gettin' a little older, so finally I got a chance to get into a nightclub where he worked at. I never will forget. It was on Independence Avenue and Truce. Upstairs. So I used to go up there and say, 'I want to see Mr. Slam Stewart. I got some cigars for him.
